requirements.syllabus_text: define government economic policy
requirements.demand: Recall: define; distinguish aim from instrument
requirements.adequate_response: Actions/decisions by government to influence the economy toward aims (e.g. employment, price stability)
requirements.exam_evidence: none found as a stand-alone question; underpins fiscal/monetary questions (2021 P2 Q(c), 2023 P2 Q3(a))
requirements.why: V-001 and V-003 plus J-002 give definition then aim/instrument progression.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss the aims of government policy and why they should be achieved - full employment - prevention of inflation - economic growth - redistribution of income - balance of payments stability
requirements.demand: Define each aim; explain why desirable; discuss conflicts/trade-offs (evaluate)
requirements.adequate_response: Define the five aims; give a reason each matters; recognise conflict (growth vs inflation, spending vs BoP)
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P2 Q2(b) why keep prices stable [7]; 2022 P2 Q(c) aims and population growth [evaluate]; 2024 P2 Q(d) growth always desirable; 2024 P1 Q16 aim from lower spending (ER: learners wrote unemployment, answer was price stability); 2023 P2 Q1(e) fiscal and equality
requirements.gap: No card on why price stability/redistribution/BoP stability matter in plain terms; no card on conflict between aims (inflation vs unemployment); no 'tax aim of progressive tax' card (2021 Q10 ER)
requirements.why: V gives definitions of all five aims; J gives mechanisms and transfer cases.

requirements.syllabus_text: explain fiscal and monetary policies of the government
requirements.demand: Define; classify instruments; distinguish; state instruments (taxation, spending; interest rate, money supply)
requirements.adequate_response: Fiscal = government spending and taxation; monetary = central bank interest rates/money supply/credit; classify a measure correctly
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P2 Q(c) describe both [4] (ER: monetary confused with fiscal); 2023 P2 Q3(a)(i) distinguish [4]; 2024 P1 Q15 two fiscal instruments (ER: tariff not accepted alone)
requirements.gap: No explicit 'list two fiscal instruments' card (2024 Q15); no 'govt policies to reduce inflation' (2024 P1 Q23c)
requirements.why: V definitions and reverse misconception; J classification and tax-cut leakage.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe the different types of taxes
requirements.demand: Define; identify; compute average rates to classify
requirements.adequate_response: Define direct, indirect, progressive, proportional, regressive; name Namibian examples; classify from figures
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q10 (ER: partially answered, direct taxes), Q11 aim/application progressive; 2022 P1 Q19 proportional tax meaning and example
requirements.gap: No card on aim of progressive tax (more equal income distribution; 2021 Q11a); no 'work out which tax type from figures' for indirect (VAT regressive)
requirements.repetition: proportional cluster V-012, V-033, J-020, J-028, J-035; definitions duplicated
requirements.why: V real Namibian examples and clear definitions; J numeric progressive/regressive templates.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss how taxes are used by the government to influence business activities and the role of the budget
requirements.demand: Explain tax effects on business; define budget; deficit/surplus/balanced; evaluate
requirements.adequate_response: Explain how tax changes alter demand/costs for firms; define budget; state when deficit/surplus occurs; budget not trade balance
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q12 budget surplus (ER: referred to imports/exports); 2022 P1 Q20 define budget deficit (ER: defined trade deficit); 2023 P2 Q1(e) assess fiscal policy [9]
requirements.gap: No card on budget surplus/balanced budget; none on taxes on businesses (corporate tax cut, VAT/excise raising costs, taxing demerit goods); none on subsidies
requirements.why: V budget definition and numeric deficit; J misconception wording; both need new cards for business taxes and surplus.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe how the government can use the interest rate to influence business activity
requirements.demand: Explain chain: interest rate to borrowing cost to investment/demand; effects on savers, exchange rate
requirements.adequate_response: Higher rate: borrowing dearer, investment and spending fall; lower rate opposite; savers/exchange rate effects
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q13 exchange rate effect (ER: poorly answered); 2023 P2 Q3(a)(ii),(b),(c) fall in rate on living standard, savers, businesses; 2024 P1 Q23(b) high interest on businesses [7+]
requirements.gap: No card on effect on savers; none on exchange rate/foreign deposits (2021 Q13; ER wrong); none on consumers' borrowing and spending
requirements.why: V chain and J numeric/indirect customer effect; both add peg or fixed-loan complexity that should be trimmed.

requirements.syllabus_text: explain the reasons for government's intervention in business
requirements.demand: Explain why government intervenes: externalities, information, monopoly, equity
requirements.adequate_response: Name and explain at least external costs, consumer information gaps, monopoly power, worker protection
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q16 why govt controls monopolies (ER partially answered); 2021 Q15 traders must give credit information
requirements.gap: No monopoly control card (V notes and 2021 Q16); no merit/demerit or public goods reason; V lacks externality
requirements.why: J supplies externality and information reasons; V supplies safety benefit.

requirements.syllabus_text: explain how the government controls production of goods and services
requirements.demand: Explain methods: regulation, licensing, price controls, subsidies, quotas
requirements.adequate_response: Explain rules/standards, inspection, price ceilings/floors with effects
requirements.exam_evidence: 2023 P1 Q2 price control market vs command; 2024 P1 Q23(c) price controls to reduce inflation; 2020 P2 Q1(b)(c) minimum wage diagram
requirements.gap: No cards on subsidies, quotas/licences (in V notes)
requirements.why: V adds checked max/min price diagrams; J adds enforcement gap.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss how consumers are protected in Namibia
requirements.demand: Describe and discuss Namibian protections and complaint routes
requirements.adequate_response: Name Namibian bodies/laws (verify) and explain how they protect consumers; limitations
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q15 compulsory credit-scheme information (ER: poorly answered)
requirements.gap: No card names a real Namibian institution (e.g. Namibian Competition Commission, Namibian Standards Institution, CRAN, NAMFISA): needs verified facts. 2021 Q15 (credit terms disclosure) uncovered
requirements.why: Both generic; V notes are richer than V cards.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss how employees are protected by the State
requirements.demand: Describe and discuss legal protections (minimum wage, Labour Act, safety, unions)
requirements.adequate_response: Explain minimum wage effects (diagram), health and safety inspection, Labour Act conditions
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P2 Q1 minimum wage [4+7+9] (ER: learners thought minimum wage below current wage; shifted curves)
requirements.gap: No card on Labour Act basic conditions, unions, health and safety law (V notes only)
requirements.why: V min wage cluster matches the best-evidenced exam topic.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss how the government can protect people with HIV and AIDS at the workplace
requirements.demand: Explain non-discrimination and confidentiality protections
requirements.adequate_response: No unfair discrimination; confidentiality of status; training/counselling; dignity; may continue working while able
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q14 two protections [2] (ER well answered); 2023 P2 Q2(b) HIV/AIDS effects
requirements.gap: No card on confidentiality of status, no compulsory testing, counselling/information; Namibian law basis (Labour Act 2007 s5) not stated
requirements.why: V basic cards plus J confidentiality evaluation (moved to extended).

requirements.syllabus_text: define retail price index and show its simple calculation
requirements.demand: Define; calculate index from basket; interpret changes; weights
requirements.adequate_response: Index = current basket cost/base cost x100; points vs percent; weights in basket
requirements.exam_evidence: 2022 P1 Q Section B (a) how RPI measured [4], (b) weights ER; 2024 P2 Q3(c) measurement [7] with weights, base year 100; 2022 P1 Q13 real income
requirements.gap: No weighted-index card (V notes have one); no card on base year purpose; real disposable income calculation (2022 Q13)
requirements.why: Both bank cards unweighted; need weights.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe different types of inflation
requirements.demand: Define inflation; distinguish demand-pull, cost-push, monetary
requirements.adequate_response: Demand-pull, cost-push (wage-push, imported), monetary (money supply)
requirements.exam_evidence: 2024 P2 Q3(a),(b) define and types; 2023 P1 Q16 wage rise cost-push; 2022 P1 Q(c) demand/cost-push causes of falling food inflation
requirements.gap: wage-push example card; imported inflation and weaker N$ link
requirements.why: J lacks monetary inflation; V covers all three types.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss the consequences of inflation
requirements.demand: Explain effects on groups; evaluate positive vs negative
requirements.adequate_response: Fixed-income earners, savers, borrowers, exporters, redistribution
requirements.exam_evidence: 2022 P1 Q(d) evaluate positive impact [evaluate] (ER: learners listed only negatives); 2023 P1 Q17 borrowers; 2024 P2 Q3(d) why government concerned [7]; 2020 P2 Q2(b) why keep prices stable
requirements.gap: No card for savers/creditors, exports and competitiveness, redistribution, menu costs; core borrower-benefit card (V-010 needs rewrite)
requirements.repetition: pension/borrower repeated across V-P04, J-P03, J-P02
requirements.why: V has the exam-aligned borrower essay; J has quantified pension.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe and discuss the changing patterns and levels of employment
requirements.demand: Describe and discuss: read sector counts, compute share vs level, interpret why they diverge; Namibian patterns (sectors, formal/informal, youth).
requirements.adequate_response: Compute sector shares from data, distinguish level (count) from pattern (distribution), explain that a count can rise while share falls.
requirements.exam_evidence: No direct sector-share question 2020-2024 found. Adjacent: 2023 P1 Q20 (earlier retirement reduces working population; ER: many wrote about the unemployment rate); 2024 P2 Q5 stem quotes Namibian unemployment 21.7% (context only).
requirements.gap: Neither bank covers Namibian patterns of employment (shift between primary/secondary/tertiary, informal sector, youth and regional differences) or the working-population/labour-force vocabulary tested in 2023 P1 Q20.
requirements.repetition: Level-vs-share is repeated 5 times (V 001-003, P01(a); J 001, P02).
requirements.why: J:001 is the best numerical card; V:013/V:P03 supply employment/labour-force vocabulary.

requirements.syllabus_text: investigate the reasons for unemployment
requirements.demand: Identify and explain cause types and apply them to cases; explain reasons for high unemployment in Namibia.
requirements.adequate_response: Name the type (cyclical, structural, seasonal, frictional), describe it (lack of total demand; mismatch; recurring; job search) and apply to a case.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P2 Q2(c) type identified, ER: could not describe cyclical (general); 2022 P2 Q2 structural vs seasonal; 2023 P2 Q5(a)(i) cyclical, ER: confused with structural, omitted 'total demand'; 2024 P2 Q5(a) define unemployment (ER: omit 'seeking/cannot find'), Q5(b) reasons (ER: learners named types, not reasons; scheme: few jobs, lack of industries, capital-intensive technology, lack of skills).
requirements.gap: Neither tests 'outline reasons why unemployment is high in a country' (lack of industries, capital-intensive mining, skills shortage, population growth, youth); J has no seasonal/frictional card; V has no case-classification card (fixed by revising V:020).
requirements.repetition: Cyclical mechanism appears in V:005, J:003 and both P-items.
requirements.why: V covers all four types and the exam definition; J:004 is the better case-identification card.

requirements.syllabus_text: investigate the consequences of unemployment
requirements.demand: Investigate consequences for households, firms, government, economy and society.
requirements.adequate_response: State and develop at least two linked consequences (lost income and spending; lost output; loss of skills; benefits and lower tax revenue; social effects).
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P2 Q2(d) 7 marks (ER: learners discussed other things; scheme: loss of skills, cost of benefits, lower GDP); 2022 P2 Q2 consequences (loss of earnings, benefits, lower GDP, health/social); 2024 P2 Q5(c) why government concerned (ER: could not link to the economy).
requirements.gap: No card on government consequences (benefit cost, lower tax receipts) or social consequences (crime, health, depression, emigration), both in 2022 and 2024 schemes.
requirements.repetition: Household earnings loss appears in V:008, V:009, J:005, J:P02.
requirements.why: V:008 (wider economy) + J:005 (households, long-term skills) are complementary; both lack government and social angles.

requirements.syllabus_text: investigate remedies to unemployment
requirements.demand: Investigate/evaluate remedies matched to cause.
requirements.adequate_response: Match remedy to cause (training for structural; demand support for cyclical; job information for frictional), state a limit and a condition.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2023 P2 Q5(b) 7 marks methods to reduce unemployment (ER: learners wrote about Covid, listed, did not analyse); 2024 P2 Q5 'structural changes needed to create jobs'.
requirements.gap: Named policies are missing: fiscal/monetary demand support, investment incentives, subsidies and support for small business, regional/labour mobility help, education reform. J says 'demand support' without naming tools; V covers training and vacancy information only.
requirements.repetition: Training remedy appears in 7 items (V:010, 012, P01, P04; J:007, P02, P03).
requirements.why: J:P03 supplies cause-matched cases; V:011/V:010 supply benefit and limit cards.

requirements.syllabus_text: define Gross Domestic Product, Gross National Product and National Income
requirements.demand: Define and distinguish three aggregates; apply the GNP adjustment.
requirements.adequate_response: GDP: value of final goods/services produced within a country in a period; GNP = GDP + income received from abroad - income paid abroad; NI = income of factors (wages, rent, interest, profit).
requirements.exam_evidence: 2022 P1 Q23 outline GDP vs GNP, 2 marks (ER: most defined GDP, not GNP); 2020 P2 Q2(a) GDP at constant prices, 3 marks (ER: ignore inflation); 2020 P1 Q18 formula for GDP per capita (ER: definition given, not formula); 2023 P2 ER 'GDP/GNI / population'.
requirements.gap: No card for GDP per capita formula (2020 P1 Q18) or GDP at constant prices (partly V:007).
requirements.repetition: GDP/GNP appear in 2 definitions + 2 'identify' cards per bank.
requirements.why: V definition cards have 2-mark exam-style splits and calculation; J's are 1 mark.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe the different methods of calculating the national income
requirements.demand: Describe three methods; avoid double counting.
requirements.adequate_response: Output (value added), income (wages, rent, interest, profit; no transfers), expenditure (C+I+G+X-M); methods give same total, not summed.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P2 Q5(a) identify methods used to calculate GDP, 3 marks.
requirements.gap: Listing all three methods in one answer (J:008 revised); no calculation using the expenditure formula.
requirements.repetition: Output method defined/applied 3x in each bank.
requirements.why: V definitions + V:005/006; J:P02 reconciles all three with numbers; J:012/014 add exclusions.

requirements.syllabus_text: explain reasons for measuring the national income
requirements.demand: Explain reasons; distinguish real and nominal; limits of totals.
requirements.adequate_response: Give at least two reasons (planning, compare living standards over time and between countries, sector contribution, growth) and explain real vs nominal and per-person limits.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P1 Q20 two reasons (ER: poorly answered); 2021 P2 Q5(b) why government calculates GDP; 2020 P2 Q2(a) constant prices.
requirements.gap: Neither bank has a card that lists reasons (as printed in V note and tested in 2020 P1 Q20); V:008 revised fixes it. No real-GDP calculation although V note teaches it.
requirements.repetition: Real-vs-nominal repeated: V:007, V:008, V:P02(g), J:015, J:P01.
requirements.why: V:009/V:P04 for welfare limits; J:015 for real series; reasons card to be authored.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe the changing patterns of exports and imports and the effects on the balance of payments
requirements.demand: Describe export/import patterns; distinguish balance of trade, current account and BoP; place transactions in accounts.
requirements.adequate_response: Define balance of trade/BoP, compute balance, place investment in capital account, tourism in invisible exports.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q18 balance of trade (ER: learners wrote BoP structure); 2023 P1 Q18 Angolan purchase of Namibian company: capital account (ER: learners said current); 2024 P1 Q24(a) define BoP (ER: learners wrote balance of trade); 2024 P2 Q6(a) tourism: invisible/export of services/credit item.
requirements.gap: No card on tourism earnings in the current account (2024 P2 Q6a); J has no definition of BoP or current account; 'patterns' (composition, partners) only in J:002 and the V note.
requirements.repetition: Goods-vs-BoP confusion has 3 cards (V:016, J:011, V:P01/J:P02).
requirements.why: V covers BoP/current account vocabulary the exam tests; J:001 adds a good widening-deficit calculation.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss exchange rates and give reasons for their fluctuations
requirements.demand: Define and calculate exchange rate; explain causes (demand/supply of currency, interest, inflation, tourism, speculation).
requirements.adequate_response: Define appreciation/depreciation, convert currencies, list/explain at least three causes.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q13 interest rate rise (ER: poorly answered); 2020 P1 Q21 three causes (ER: well answered); 2021 P1 Q20, 2022 P1 Q6 define exchange rate; 2024 P1 Q17 US$30,000 x 17.80 (ER: some omit N$); 2023 P2 Q5(a)(ii) define depreciation, Q5(c) evaluate depreciation; 2024 P2 Q6(b) factors incl. low exchange rate.
requirements.gap: No depreciation definition; no list of 3 causes; no N$ conversion in both directions (US$ to N$ and N$ to US$); peg claim needs a verified statement. Each bank covers 2-3 causes only (export demand, interest).
requirements.repetition: Currency-demand mechanism: V:005 and J:003 are near-duplicates.
requirements.why: V:004-006 revised for definitions and causes; J:004 revised for conversion.

requirements.syllabus_text: demonstrate the simple application of absolute and comparative advantage in trade
requirements.demand: Apply opportunity cost to data; distinguish absolute and comparative advantage; trade terms.
requirements.adequate_response: Compute opportunity costs from output data, name the comparative-advantage producer for each good, state that absolute advantage in both does not prevent gains, and show terms between the two costs benefit both.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P1 Q17 define absolute advantage (ER: learners wrote comparative); 2023 P1 Q19 describe comparative advantage (ER: learners wrote absolute). No numerical item 2020-2024.
requirements.gap: None for printed bullet; optional numerical trade-terms calculation.
requirements.repetition: Same data set reused by 6 V items and 5 J items (A 2:1, B 1:1 structure identical).
requirements.why: J definitions + J:005 calc on V data + V:P03 for terms/gain.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe developed and developing economies and reasons for different stages of development
requirements.demand: Describe characteristics and explain reasons for different stages.
requirements.adequate_response: Define developed/developing country (GDP per head etc.), list characteristics, explain reasons for stages (capital, skills, infrastructure, institutions, resources, history/debt).
requirements.exam_evidence: 2024 P1 Q19 define developed country (ER: need GDP per head); 2024 P2 Q2(c) characteristics of developing country, 7 marks (ER: learners listed, max 3); 2022 P2 Q6(b) analyse why classified developing; 2021 P2 Q6(b) Switzerland vs Mali; 2023 P1 Q22 table of birth/death/life expectancy/infant mortality.
requirements.gap: Neither has: characteristics list of developing/developed countries; reasons for different stages (colonial history, debt, institutions, trade); interpretation of a data table to rank standard of living (2023 P1 Q22).
requirements.repetition: Living-standard/indicator point appears in V:002, J:001, J:004.
requirements.why: J:003/005 revised for exam definitions; V:002/003 for reasoning.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss problems and consequences for developing countries as they develop
requirements.demand: Discuss problems of development (urbanisation, unemployment, pollution, pressure on services).
requirements.adequate_response: Identify and develop problems and say which are linked to development (e.g. urbanisation).
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P2 Q6(c) problems as country becomes more developed, 7 marks (ER: not well answered, 3/7); 2024 P2 Q2(d) evaluate problems; 2021 P1 Q22 two negative effects of urbanisation in Namibia; 2020 P2 Q6(a) why people migrate to urban areas.
requirements.gap: Neither tests reasons for rural-urban migration (push/pull) or a list of problems (unemployment, informal settlements, crime, pollution, inequality, brain drain).
requirements.repetition: V:005 and V:006 are different angles (pressure vs benefit).
requirements.why: V gives flashcard-sized urbanisation cards; J:007 is extended-response.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe the factors that affect population growth (birth rate, death rate, fertility rate, net migration) and reasons for rates of growth in Namibia and other countries
requirements.demand: Define and compute rates; explain reasons for different growth rates in countries.
requirements.adequate_response: Define birth, death, fertility, net migration; compute natural increase and net migration; explain causes of high/low growth (family planning, education, medicine, immigration, culture).
requirements.exam_evidence: 2023 P1 Q21 net migration, 2 marks; 2021 P2 Q6(a) natural growth, birth and death rate (ER: learners gave factors not natural rate); 2020 P2 Q6(b) why control growth (ER: listed problems of over-population instead); 2022 P2 Q6(a) reasons high growth in Nigeria, Q6(c) effects on government aims (ER: only negatives).
requirements.gap: No card on reasons for high or low growth rates in Namibia and other countries; no natural-growth-rate calculation (birth rate - death rate per 1,000 = %); no Namibian data (must be dated and verified if added).
requirements.repetition: Natural vs total change: 8 cards (V 007, 008, 009, 017; J 008, 017, 020, 009).
requirements.why: V:P01/P02 and V definitions; J:008, J:015 for calculation and TFR interpretation.

requirements.syllabus_text: discuss the effects of changing size and structure of population on an economy
requirements.demand: Discuss effects of population size/age structure on output, spending, public services.
requirements.adequate_response: Explain effects of more children, more working-age people, more elderly; dependency; conditions for gains.
requirements.exam_evidence: 2023 P1 Q20 earlier retirement age reduces working population; 2022 P2 Q6(c) effect of high growth on government aims.
requirements.gap: Ageing population (pensions, health costs, labour shortage) and falling working population (2023 P1 Q20) are not covered by either bank.
requirements.repetition: Working-age potential vs outcome: V:012, V:P04, J:018, J:019, J:P03.
requirements.why: V cards plus J:P03 two-case evaluation.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe simple measures and indicators of comparative living standards
requirements.demand: Remember and apply: name/define indicators and compute or interpret per-head figures
requirements.adequate_response: Names several indicators, defines them, computes per head, notes averages hide distribution
requirements.exam_evidence: 2024 P1 Q18, Q20; 2023 P1 Q22; 2023 P2 Q1(a); 2021 P2 (b). ER: learners compare growth instead of living standards.
requirements.gap: Interpreting a table of indicators (2023 P1 Q22).
requirements.repetition: Total-v-per-head repeated in V-014, J-009, V-P01.
requirements.why: V has indicator definitions, J has calculation.

requirements.syllabus_text: describe differences in living standards and discuss reasons for disparities within nations and between nations, both developed and developing countries
requirements.demand: Describe and explain causes of disparities
requirements.adequate_response: Gives reasons within and between countries with developed/developing contrast
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P2 Q(b) Switzerland v Mali (7 marks); ER lists GDP, health, education, stability, capital.
requirements.gap: No between-nations card in either bank.
requirements.why: Neither covers developed v developing.

requirements.syllabus_text: explain the effect of Information Technology on living standards
requirements.demand: Explain benefits and limits of IT
requirements.adequate_response: Access/time gains, digital divide, costs
requirements.exam_evidence: 2021 P2 (c)(d); 2023 P2 (c). ER: learners miss negatives.
requirements.gap: IT access developed v developing; negatives (data cost, privacy).
requirements.why: V-P03 is the only extended IT item.

requirements.syllabus_text: social costs* and benefits, private costs and benefits (*Social costs are equal to the sum of private costs and external costs)
requirements.demand: Define, calculate and judge
requirements.adequate_response: Social = private + external; judgement includes third parties
requirements.gap: Standalone define social/external cost; external benefits; effect of policy on private cost (2023 Q24).
requirements.why: J calc plus V defs.

requirements.syllabus_text: short/long term costs and benefits
requirements.demand: Compare effects over time
requirements.adequate_response: Identifies immediate vs later effects and judges
requirements.exam_evidence: none found as a standalone question
requirements.gap: A basic explain-timing card.
requirements.why: Thin everywhere.

requirements.syllabus_text: conserving resources versus exploiting resources
requirements.demand: Distinguish and assess
requirements.adequate_response: Use is not overuse; weighs future v present
requirements.exam_evidence: 2020 P2 (d) 7 marks.
requirements.why: V has recall plus eval.

requirements.syllabus_text: free trade versus protection
requirements.demand: Define methods and weigh
requirements.adequate_response: Tariff, quota, embargo, subsidy; gains and costs
requirements.gap: Reasons for protection (2023 Q23) and for free trade.
requirements.why: J lacks definitions.

requirements.syllabus_text: public expenditure versus private expenditure
